decision: How should the phone layout (below 700px) cut length so a parent can scan it, with desktop unchanged?
primary_axis: page structure on phones: density vs disclosure vs order
invariants: same copy and sections in the code
desktop and tablet (700px and up) unchanged
shared: shorter hero photo, no drifting-photo banner, closing keeps claim and buttons only, FAQ shows 6 questions

options.bet: Tighten in place: same order and sections; How becomes numbered rows without photos; Why cards fit their text; Included drops its photo
options.benefit: Lowest risk; nothing moves, every point stays
options.risk: Feels like the same long page, only shorter

options.bet: Swipe decks: How, Why, Included and Compare become one-row carousels with the next card peeking
options.benefit: Shortest page (8.8 screens); keeps the step photos
options.cost: Most cards are hidden behind a swipe; many visitors never swipe
options.risk: Value points and the competitor panels go unseen; price comparison reads as one panel

options.bet: Decision first: cut what repeats (Why, promise cards), then How -> Included -> Compare -> Pricing
options.benefit: Every remaining point is visible without a swipe; price on screen 6
options.cost: Why section is not shown on phones; order differs from desktop
options.risk: Loses the 'Real paper. Real pencil.' and 'Master it, then move on.' lines on phones unless folded elsewhere
